newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Wall Street holds key for Belgian shares.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street holds key for Belgian shares.

text.p: The Dow Jones's reaction to the U.S. policy-making FOMC's decision on interest rates, expected later Tuesday, will set the tone for Belgian shares on Wednesday, dealers said.
The Bel-20 index .BFX closed down just 0.18 point at 1,750.46 in cautious trading on Tuesday. Total Belgian share volume was a moderate 1.5 billion francs.

"If there's no change in U.S. rates I think the market here will be down tomorrow," said one dealer. "It means there will need to be a bigger hike in rates later." He expected the Fed funds rate to be raised by 25 basis points.

A buoyant Belgian bond market, with the 10-year yield spread over Bunds narrowing, gave some support to rangebound shares, and higher-than-expected September U.S. consumer confidence data left the market unchanged in late afternoon.
"It was a very quiet, very careful day," said a trader.

Tractebel was the most heavily traded stock in value terms, ending 0.3 percent down at 14,700 francs with 14,516 shares changing hands. Kredietbank NV gained one percent to 10,150 francs after tumbling 3.8 percent on Monday and Cockerill Sambre, upgraded from "sell" to "hold" by Bank Degroof, fell 0.8 percent to 129 francs.
